title: Allocation-tiling KV Window Sequencer: continuous-batcher tuning for mixed-length prompts
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: Our continuous-batching runtime handles highly skewed mixed-length workloads (short prompts followed by long responses, and vice-versa). Current behaviour causes suboptimal GPU slab fragmentation and KV cache pressure when short and long sequences interleave, increasing mutex contention and causing 95th latency regressions for bursty conversational traffic.

Objective: Introduce an allocation-tiling + KV window sequencing strategy in the continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce long-tailed latency and GPU memory fragmentation while preserving high token throughput for long sequences. The feature will: (1) group slots into allocation tiles that bias co-location by similar peak sequence length, (2) sequence KV prefetch/eviction in windowed epochs to reduce cross-talk between short/long workloads, and (3) adapt tile boundaries dynamically based on a lightweight heatmap and recent length histogram.

Success metrics (targeted):
- 95th percentile generation latency for short prompt bursts: reduce from 220ms to <= 120ms on p4d-equivalent nodes.
- GPU memory fragmentation metric (slab free ratio variance): reduce by >= 20% across 1-hour mixed-length traces.
- Net token/sec throughput: <= 5% regression for long-heavy workloads, ideally neutral or improved.
- KV residency churn: reduce eviction rate by >= 15% on mixed dialog traces.

Scope and non-goals:
- This ticket focuses on scheduler and KV-window sequencing logic in the runtime; it does not modify kernel-level quantization paths or model sharding.
- Not targeting cross-model routing or multi-tenant isolation in this iteration.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Allocation tiles: divide active batch slots into N tiles (default 4) where each tile prefers slots with similar max length. Tiles provide co-location affinity so long KV caches and attention state live on contiguous slab regions reducing fragmentation.
2) Tile scoring & rebalancing: maintain a lightweight per-tile length histogram (exponentially decayed). Rebalance thresholds run every 250ms to move hot slots between tiles if imbalance exceeds 30% to avoid micro-thrashing.
3) KV window sequencer: instead of immediate KV eviction when capacity high, run eviction/compaction in windowed epochs (configurable default 500ms) where prefetches for upcoming active tiles are prioritized and cold entries are compacted in low-load windows.
4) Prefetch heuristics: when a request is enqueued and its tile is scheduled, prefetch top-K KV shards for the tile in the next epoch to hide IO for on-disk/host-pinned caches.
5) GPU slab allocation tiling: align slab allocations so that tiles map to contiguous slab ranges; add a tile-level free list to reduce cross-tile allocation churn.
6) Safety and fallbacks: when a tile becomes overloaded, allow immediate cross-tile allocation with eviction but mark the event to trigger automatic tile split in subsequent rebalancing.

Trade-offs:
- Co-location improves fragmentation but risks localized contention if too aggressively partitioned; mitigated by adaptive rebalancing and merge heuristics.
- Windowed eviction reduces churn but may increase peak memory usage; we cap window growth and enforce hard watermarks to prevent OOMs.

Implementation plan / milestones: 
- Spike (2wk): implement a prototype tile index and simulated rebalancer inside the scheduler (in-memory only) and run replayed traces.
- Bench phase (1wk): run synthetic mixed-length traces (product logs + synthetic heavy-short bursts) on a single GPU node to validate latency/memory behaviour.
- Integration (2wk): integrate tile-to-slab mapping in allocator, implement KV window sequencer, add observability hooks.
- Canary (1wk): deploy to canary fleet (~5 nodes) behind a controlled rollout with traffic shaping.
- Gradual rollout (2-3w): step up percent of fleet with A/B metrics.

Testing and validation:
- Replayed traces: use archived customer traces and internal synthetic mixes (short-heavy, balanced, long-heavy). Include stress scenarios with rapid switching every 2-10s.
- Microbenchmarks: slab fragmentation profiler, KV eviction counters, per-tile contention and mutex hold times.
- E2E: verify request success rates and tail latencies for chat endpoints using canary traffic.
- Safety: OOM injection tests and failsafe verification for hard watermarks.

Observability & dashboards:
- New tile-level metrics: tile_length_histogram, tile_eviction_rate, tile_prefetch_latency, tile_free_slab_bytes.
- Composite dashboards: mixed-length SLO dashboard for canaries, diff view vs baseline (prior runtime).
- Alert: tile imbalance > 60% for > 1 minute triggers scheduler-ops paging.

Rollout plan and experiment design:
- Canary group will run 10% of production baseline load shaped to 50/50 short/long mixes.
- Compare 7-day rolling averages for metrics above and compute non-inferiority with 95% CI.
- If any safety guard trips, automatic rollback and postmortem.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Allocation+Tiling+and+KV+Window+Sequencer (draft)
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2379 (WIP)
- Benchmark dashboard (internal): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/continuous-batch/alloc-tiling-experiments

Open questions / decisions needed: 
- Default tile count: 2 vs 4 vs 8 — we will pick 4 for initial spike and parameterize via config.
- Window epoch size trade: 250ms vs 500ms — benchmark to pick latency/regression sweet spot.
- Prefetch budget: fixed K shards vs adaptive by tile heat — prefer adaptive but complexity trade-offs need review.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Increased peak memory: enforce hard watermarks and admission control at the request-level.
- Scheduler correctness: add determinism tests for slot movement to avoid starvation.
- Telemetry noise: add tags to metrics to correlate by traffic mix and client id to avoid false positives.

Next steps (short):
- Aisha: finalize design doc and add microbenchmark harness (by 2026-03-13).
- Luca: land spike PR with simulated rebalancer and replayed traces (by 2026-03-24).
- Infra: reserve canary pool and create perf job templates for 1/4/8 tile configs.
